title: Morphisms of etale spaces descend along universal submersions
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Quasi-compactness of a space means that every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact, and a morphism is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Etaleness means chartwise etaleness [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], which allows nonrepresentable maps. Finite presentation means local finite presentation on scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $p:B'\to B$ be a map of quasi-separated spaces which is universally submersive: after every algebraic-space base change, its point map is surjective and has the quotient Zariski topology. For quasi-separated etale spaces $X,Y\to B$, pullback identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,Y)$ bijectively with those maps $a':X\times_BB'\to Y\times_BB'$ over $B'$ whose two pullbacks to $B'\times_BB'$ agree. In particular compatible isomorphisms descend uniquely, as do equalities of morphisms. No quasi-compactness, flatness, or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $p$, $X\to B$, or $Y\to B$.

source.place: Proposition (5.3), printed p.18, and Remark (5.2); graph proof through Corollary (A.3), printed p.35. Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_BY$, $W\prime=W\times_BB\prime$, and $r:W\prime\to W$; these products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The hypothesis on $p$ makes $|r|$ a surjective quotient map. Since $Y\times_BB\prime\to B\prime$ is a base change of the etale map $Y\to B$, it is chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], so the graph correspondence [lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph] over $B\prime$ makes the graph $G\prime$ of the given $a\prime$ an open subspace of $W\prime$. Its two inverse images on $W\prime\times_WW\prime=W\times_B(B\prime\times_BB\prime)$ agree: graph formation commutes with base change and the two maps agree by assumption. Write $A\prime=|G\prime|$ and $A=|r|(A\prime)$. For two points of $W\prime$ above the same point of $W$, [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] supplies a point of their fibre product. Equality of the two pulled-back opens therefore says that either both points belong to $A\prime$ or neither does. Hence $|r|^{-1}(A)=A\prime$. The quotient topology implies that $A$ is open.

source.place: Proposition (5.3), Remark (5.2), and Corollary (A.3), printed pp.18 and 35; graph argument expanded using Stacks Tags 03H4 and 03BZ.

proof.text: The open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives the unique open $G\subseteq W$ with point image $A$. By the image/preimage formula and detection of open subspaces by their points in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $G\times_BB\prime=G\prime$ as open subspaces of $W\prime$. Let $q:G\to X$ be projection. The open inclusion $G\to W$ is chartwise etale by [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests]. The map $W\to X$ is a base change of the etale map $Y\to B$; therefore $q$ is chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Its pullback $q\prime:G\prime\to X\prime$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph], since $G\prime$ is the graph of $a\prime$.

source.place: Proposition (5.3), Remark (5.2), and Corollary (A.3), printed pp.18 and 35; graph argument expanded using Stacks Tags 03H4 and 03BZ.

proof.text: For every algebraic-space map $T\to X$, set $G_T=G\times_XT$ and $T\prime=T\times_BB\prime$. The map $G_T\times_TT\prime\to T\prime$ is an isomorphism. Surjectivity of $|T\prime|\to|T|$ then shows directly that $|G_T|\to|T|$ is surjective. To check injectivity, put $D=G_T\times_TG_T$. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], $G_T\to T$ is etale; the graph of $1_{G_T}$ over $T$ is thus an open subspace $\Delta\subseteq D$ by [lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph]. After pullback to $T\prime$ this open is all of $D\times_TT\prime$, because $G_T\times_TT\prime\to T\prime$ is an isomorphism. The point map $|D\times_TT\prime|\to|D|$ is surjective by universal submersivity of $p$. The image/preimage identity and open-subspace detection of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] imply $|\Delta|=|D|$. Given two points of $G_T$ with the same image in $T$, the same cited node supplies a point of $D$ above them. As this point lies in the diagonal image, the two points coincide. Thus $q$ is surjective and universally injective on points.

source.place: Proposition (5.3), Remark (5.2), and Corollary (A.3), printed pp.18 and 35; graph argument expanded using Stacks Tags 03H4 and 03BZ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph] to the open $G\subseteq X\times_BY$ and the two properties just established. It says that $q:G\to X$ is an isomorphism and that $a=\operatorname{pr}_Y\circ q^{-1}$ is the unique morphism having this graph. Its pullback has graph $G\prime$ because the graph correspondence commutes with base change, so its pullback is exactly $a\prime$. Conversely any morphism over $B$ has equal pullbacks to $B\prime\times_BB\prime$, simply by associativity of pullback.

source.place: Proposition (5.3), Remark (5.2), and Corollary (A.3), printed pp.18 and 35; graph argument expanded using Stacks Tags 03H4 and 03BZ.

proof.text: If $a,b:X\to Y$ become equal over $B\prime$, [lem-sfb-space-etale-open-graph] identifies their pulled-back graphs. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], pulling back an open subspace takes its point image to the inverse image. Since $|W\prime|\to|W|$ is surjective, the two original graph images agree; the same node detects equality of the open subspaces, and the graph bijection gives $a=b$. This proves injectivity and the assertion about equalities. If $a\prime$ is an isomorphism, its inverse is compatible too, because taking inverses preserves the two pullback equalities. Apply the existence already proved with $X,Y$ interchanged to descend the inverse. The composites pull back to identities, so injectivity makes them identities over $B$. This proves the isomorphism clause.
